subject: HelioCart: urgent throughput & 5xx spike — exec attention and remediation track
messages:
From: Simon Ellis <simon.ellis@heliocart.com>
To: priya_natarajan
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency and 5xx spike impacting checkouts

Priya —

Our checkout traffic spiked at ~13:50 PDT and we saw sustained 95th-percentile latencies jump from ~220ms to >1.2s, plus a 7% 5xx error rate. This is impacting ~18% of checkout attempts and causing significant abandonment on the eastern region. We already rolled users back to a cached checkout page but need immediate mitigation and a plan for root cause.

Attached is a short span export showing increased service time around the payments service. Can your team confirm whether this is a model-serving throttling or infra scheduler backlog? We need an exec readout in the next 6 hours.

— Simon
Head of Engineering, HelioCart

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency and 5xx spike impacting checkouts

Quick summary from infra: at 13:47 we hit an uneven shard hot-spot on our GPU pool for the xform-qa model variant used by HelioCart's checkout scoring. Continuous batching queue length increased sharply, so KV-cache misses amplified tail latency. Preliminary mitigation applied:
- scaled an extra dedicated GPU pair in us-west-2 (active within 4m)
- widened model fallback to a lower-quantized variant for non-critical scoring (reduces accuracy ~1.5%)
- enabled prefix-KV prefetch for the checkout route

Early telemetry shows 95th dropping toward 480–600ms and 5xx down to ~2.2%. We need a short-term throttle policy and longer-term redispatch to an isolated pool for HelioCart traffic. Logging attached (rta-span-analysis.csv).

Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Serving Runtime
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: priya_natarajan, vivek_kulkarni, karthik_iyer
Cc: Simon Ellis <simon.ellis@heliocart.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@heliocart.com>, grace_oconnor
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency and 5xx spike impacting checkouts

Follow-up on diagnostics: the error traces map to a backlog in the GPU scheduler causing OOM evictions for large-context requests to payments-scoring. Short-term plan in the next 2 hours:
- enforce request size caps on checkout route (throttle > 8k tokens)
- enforce adaptive batching thresholds during spike windows
- route HelioCart to the reserved burst capacity we just scaled (no config change on their side)

I will open SUP-3219 with the full trace and proposed code changes. Recommend a 72-hour remediation sprint to harden autoscaling and to add a per-customer isolation knob. Attached: remediation-sprint-plan.pdf.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Software Engineer, Runtime Performance

- Containment: 5xx reduced to 0.9% by 11:30 PDT yesterday after scaling + fallback steps. Checkout latency 95th now ~420ms; still monitoring.
- Immediate mitigations completed: reserved burst pool, request-size cap, adaptive batching.
- Remediation sprint: 72-hour task force (SUP-3219) to implement scheduler fixes, per-tenant isolation toggle, and improved KV prefetch heuristics.
- Exec cadence: 30-min readout at 14:30 PDT today (calendar invite sent).

Deliverables we committed to HelioCart:
1) Post-incident timeline and annotated spans (by EOD today) — Vivek
2) Sprint plan with owners and test criteria (in 2 business days) — Neha
3) Completion ETA for isolation knob + regression tests (target 2027-05-05) — Karthik

I will run the readout and ensure exec-level artifacts for HelioCart leadership. Let me know if you need any escalation or credits; we can discuss during the call.

Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive
